summary: Elara checks on Silas during The Feast, enforcing communal warmth and vagal buffering.

interactive_features.description: A copper-lined basin for soothing stiff joints.
Provides thermal grounding against ambient cold.

narrative_prose:
The Feast that night was different. It wasn't loud. It was warm. The Stormbreaker hummed with captured energy. The Living Atlas glowed with a stable map. The Mycelial network pulsed with a gentle, rhythmic green.

Silas sat at the end of the long timber table, his knuckles pale around a brass spoon. He dragged the utensil through his bowl, tracing slow, jagged lines in the broth. His shoulders were hunched, locked in a rigid defensive posture. Third-quarter isolation often bred this specific brand of hypervigilant tension. Elara observed the tight line of his jaw and the shallow, rapid rise of his chest. His cortisol baseline was spiking. He needed an oxytocin buffer, something physical and communal, to break the autonomic loop.

She picked up a heavy earthen mug from the warming rack. The ceramic radiated a steady, comforting heat against her palms. She walked around the bench, stopping just behind his chair, and set the mug down next to his hand. He flinched. The sudden motion caused his grounded ankle wire to scrape loudly across the metal floorboards. He blinked, staring at the steaming liquid.

"I don't care if you're eighty-two years old and invented the induction baffle, Silas—your blood pressure is climbing, your fingers are stiff from cold-forging, and you are soaking those hands in warm Epsom brine for twenty minutes," she said, keeping her voice low and brisk.

Silas stared at the mug. He wrapped his hands around the warm ceramic, his jaw set in stubborn resistance before he finally brought the cup to his lips. He took a slow swallow. The rigidity in his spine softened, the ambient warmth of the Hub slowly overriding his physiological alarm state. "If you're complaining and no one is laughing, you're complaining wrong," he muttered, leaning back into his chair. Elara stood beside him, watching his breathing settle into a steady, even rhythm, before she finally stepped back into the firelight.
